source.title_on_document: Understanding ChatGPT’s impact on student-team ideation outcomes for new product development

paper_design_summary: Undergraduates in two separate sections of a one-day product development class at Brigham Young University (May and November 2024) ideated in teams for about 24 minutes using associative thinking. One section used ChatGPT (version 3.5) on a shared team laptop (22 students, 4 teams); the other used only analogue methods (17 students, 4 teams). Two instructors counted ideas, idea groups, and original ideas per class, reported per student; video-coded team behaviour and a self-report survey were also collected.

studies.label: Two class sections: ChatGPT-assisted vs analogue team ideation

assignment.what_was_assigned: Whole class section to ChatGPT-assisted or analogue ideation; one section per condition, taught in May and November 2024. The paper does not say how sections were assigned and never mentions randomization.
assignment.quote: This study was conducted with two separate sections of a product development class, taught at Brigham Young University during May and November of 2024.

arms.name: ChatGPT-assisted
arms.description: Team ideation with ChatGPT 3.5 on a team laptop with three keyboards and a wall-mounted display, plus two 1.5-minute ChatGPT demonstration videos; 2 teams of 6 and 2 teams of 5

arms.name: Analogue
arms.description: Team ideation with markers and Post-it notes only; 3 teams of 4 and 1 team of 5

participants.who: Undergraduates (first to fourth year) in a BYU product development class; about 70 percent manufacturing, mechanical, or technology engineering students; 8 teams in total
participants.quote: Thirty-nine students participated in the study. Seventeen students (3 teams of 4 students and 1 team of 5 students) participated in the class focused on analogue ideation. Twenty-two students (2 teams of 6 students and 2 teams of 5 students)

ai_tool.how_used: Each team shared one laptop running ChatGPT, with three input keyboards and the session shown on a wall-mounted television; used for free association (random word lists) and goal-directed association (question-and-answer prompts)

task.description: Team associative-thinking ideation (free and goal-directed association) for new product ideas addressing each team's self-identified product problem; ideas documented on Post-it notes

outcomes.name: Fluency (ideas per student)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Two instructors counted each team's ideas after removing ambiguous or incomplete ideas and merging identical ones; class totals divided by class size

contrasts.reported: Ideas per student: Analogue (n = 17) 4.8 vs ChatGPT (n = 22) 2.0; no SD, SE, or test reported

outcomes.name: Flexibility (idea groups per student)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Two instructors grouped each team's ideas by affinity mapping and counted the groups; class totals divided by class size

contrasts.reported: Idea groups per student: Analogue (n = 17) 1.8 vs ChatGPT (n = 22) 1.0; no SD, SE, or test reported

outcomes.name: Originality (original ideas per student)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Two product-development instructors counted ideas judged novel, unexpected, or unique in the design domain (described as Consensual Assessment Technique); class totals divided by class size

contrasts.reported: Original ideas per student: Analogue (n = 17) 0.3 vs ChatGPT (n = 22) 0.2; no SD, SE, or test reported

eligibility.reason: 39 students analyzed across both arms (17 analogue, 22 ChatGPT; PDF p. 2 (3282), Section 2.1; p. 5 (3285), Table 1), below 50. Conditions were delivered to two separate class sections taught in May and November 2024, one section per condition, with no random-assignment procedure reported (PDF p. 2 (3282), Section 2 Method); the comparison is coded quasi_people. Idea, idea-group, and original-idea counts are scored on the output (PDF p. 4 (3284), Section 2.3.1; p. 5 (3285), Table 1). Retain as observational context evidence, excluded from the core pooled dataset (creativity-codebook.md, Section 3; form-spec.md, Field notes for design_class). The report-only rule for randomized experiments with fewer than 50 participants does not apply to this class comparison.

one_line_finding: Per student, the analogue section (n = 17) produced 4.8 ideas, 1.8 idea groups, and 0.3 original ideas versus 2.0, 1.0, and 0.2 for the ChatGPT section (n = 22), with no test statistics (p. 5, Table 1).
